subject.title: api_key auth: MRU sticky ordering + silent 402 failover

question: Should OpenClaw keep oldest-first round-robin as the default for API-key auth profiles, or add/choose an MRU or failover-only policy for users with quota-backed backup keys?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve round-robin, while the requested change would alter provider auth selection semantics and may add public config surface.

options.title: Add explicit compatible policy
options.body: Keep current round-robin as the default and add a maintainer-approved explicit MRU/failover-only policy only after live 402 proof and docs are ready.

options.title: Flip API-key default to MRU
options.body: Make API-key profiles prefer the last successful key by default, accepting possible surprise for users relying on load distribution.

options.title: Decline MRU and document current controls
options.body: Keep round-robin only, document explicit auth.order and cooldown behavior, and limit this issue to verified 402 classifier gaps.

recommendation.title: Add explicit compatible policy
recommendation.body: Keep current round-robin as the default and add a maintainer-approved explicit MRU/failover-only policy only after live 402 proof and docs are ready.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has direct history on the lastGood test/policy surface and is the best available owner for the product/config compatibility choice.
